description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian classic known for its incredibly rich, creamy tomato-based sauce. Tender pieces of marinated chicken are simmered in a luscious gravy, offering a delightful balance of sweet and tangy flavors. This iconic dish promises a comforting and unforgettable culinary experience, perfect for any special occasion or a hearty lunch.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a bowl, combine chicken cubes with plain yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until the chicken is browned on all sides and mostly cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add another tablespoon of butter. Add chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Mixture
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato puree, soaked cashews (drained), and sugar. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 10-12 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Blend the Sauce
instructions.text: Remove the bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods (if desired, for a smoother texture). Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender or use an immersion blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. If the sauce is too thick, add a splash of water or chicken broth.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the smooth sauce to the pan. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter and stir until melted. Stir in the heavy cream and crushed Kasuri Methi. Add the cooked chicken back into the sauce. Simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the sauce flavors and heat through. Adjust salt and sugar if needed.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve hot with naan bread, roti, or basmati rice. Enjoy your homemade authentic Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani!

tips: For a deeper flavor, marinate the chicken overnight. The yogurt helps tenderize the chicken beautifully.
Soaking cashews is crucial for a smooth, rich sauce. If you dont have cashews, almonds can be used as a substitute for creaminess.
Always blend the sauce until perfectly smooth. A fine mesh sieve can be used after blending for an extra silky texture, especially if you leave in the whole spices.
article:
Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: The Quintessential Indian Lunch Recipe

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a dish that needs little introduction. Revered globally for its luscious, creamy texture and subtly spiced tomato gravy, it stands as a pillar of Indian cuisine. Originating from the bustling streets of Delhi, this culinary masterpiece has captivated palates worldwide, cementing its status as a go-to comfort food and an absolute favorite for an indulgent Indian lunch. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook looking to explore the rich tapestry of Indian flavors, mastering Butter Chicken is a rewarding journey. This article will guide you through crafting the perfect Murgh Makhani, ensuring a delectable experience right in your own kitchen.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

At its heart, Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani as it's known in Hindi, translates to "chicken with butter" – a name that perfectly encapsulates its rich, velvety character. This iconic dish features tender pieces of chicken, often marinated in yogurt and spices, then grilled or pan-fried, before being simmered in a silken tomato-based gravy. The gravy itself is a symphony of flavors, combining the sweetness of tomatoes, the warmth of aromatic spices, the richness of butter and cream, and a hint of tang. It’s known for its mild heat, making it accessible to a wide range of palates, yet its depth of flavor is profoundly satisfying. Created in the 1950s by Kundan Lal Jaggi, one of the founders of Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi, Butter Chicken was born out of a desire to use leftover tandoori chicken in a new, appealing way. The result was a culinary revolution that has since become synonymous with celebratory meals and hearty Indian lunches.

## Ingredients You Need

To create the magic of Butter Chicken, you’ll need a selection of fresh ingredients and essential Indian spices.

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*  500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*  1/2 cup plain yogurt
*  1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*  1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*  1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*  1 teaspoon garam masala
*  Salt to taste

**For the Silky Gravy:**
*  4 tablespoons unsalted butter (don't skimp!)
*  1 large onion, finely chopped
*  1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*  1 (800g) can crushed tomatoes or 4-5 ripe tomatoes, pureed
*  1/4 cup cashew pieces, soaked in warm water for 15 minutes
*  1/2 cup heavy cream (plus extra for garnish)
*  1 tablespoon kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), lightly crushed
*  1 teaspoon sugar (to balance acidity)
*  1 teaspoon red chili powder
*  1 teaspoon garam masala
*  Salt to taste
*  2-3 green cardamom pods (optional, for aroma)
*  1/2 cup water or chicken broth (as needed for consistency)

**For Garnish:**
*  Fresh coriander leaves, chopped
*  A swirl of heavy cream

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Crafting your own Butter Chicken is a joyful process that yields incredible results. Follow these steps for a restaurant-quality dish.

**1. Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring each piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, for maximum flavor.

**2. Cook the Chicken:** Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F), or a grill pan on medium-high heat. Skewer the marinated chicken or arrange it on a baking tray. Grill, pan-fry, or bake until the chicken is cooked through and slightly charred in places, about 10-15 minutes. Set aside.

**3. Prepare the Gravy Base:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and optional cardamom pods, cooking for another minute until fragrant.

**4. Build the Tomato Foundation:** Pour in the crushed tomatoes. Add the red chili powder, garam masala, and salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-15 minutes, allowing the tomatoes to break down and the sauce to thicken slightly. The oil should start to separate from the mixture.

**5. Create the Smooth Puree:** Remove the pot from heat. Carefully transfer the tomato mixture to a blender. Add the soaked cashews (drained). Blend until completely smooth. For an extra silky texture, strain the puree through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot, pressing down on the solids. Discard any fibrous residue.

**6. Finish the Gravy:** Return the pot to medium-low heat. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter, the kasuri methi, and sugar. Stir well until the butter melts and combines. Pour in the heavy cream and a little water or broth if the gravy is too thick. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken to your desired consistency.

**7. Combine and Serve:** Gently add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering gravy. Stir to coat the chicken completely. Simmer for another 2-3 minutes, just long enough for the chicken to heat through and absorb the flavors of the gravy. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Garnish generously with fresh coriander and a swirl of cream before serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that perfect, restaurant-quality Butter Chicken is all about paying attention to a few key details:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't rush the marination process. The longer the chicken soaks in the yogurt and spices, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal.
*   **The Power of Butter:** This is Butter Chicken, so don't be shy with the butter! It's crucial for the rich flavor and smooth texture.
*   **Smooth Gravy is a Must:** Blending the gravy base thoroughly is essential. For an incredibly luxurious, silky texture, don't skip the straining step after blending.
*   **Kasuri Methi Magic:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi) are non-negotiable. They impart a unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor that is characteristic of authentic Murgh Makhani. Lightly toast them in a dry pan for a few seconds before crushing them in your palm to release their oils.
*   **Balance is Everything:** The sugar in the recipe isn't just for sweetness; it balances the acidity of the tomatoes. Taste and adjust to your preference.
*   **Low and Slow:** After adding the cream, simmer the gravy gently over low heat. This allows the flavors to deepen and prevents the cream from splitting.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs beautifully with a variety of Indian breads and rice. For a truly satisfying Indian lunch experience, consider these accompaniments:

*   **Naan Bread:** Soft, fluffy naan is perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich gravy. Garlic naan or butter naan are particularly good choices.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or aromatic jeera (cumin) rice provides a wonderful contrast to the creamy sauce.
*   **Roti or Paratha:** These whole wheat flatbreads offer a healthier alternative to naan.
*   **Cooling Sides:** A simple cucumber raita (yogurt dip) or a fresh green salad can provide a refreshing counterpoint to the richness of the Butter Chicken. Sliced red onions marinated in vinegar are also a classic accompaniment.

## Variations and Substitutions

While classic Butter Chicken is a beloved staple, there are many ways to adapt this recipe to suit different dietary needs or preferences:

*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** Replace the chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, or mixed vegetables like cauliflower and peas. Cook the paneer or tofu separately until lightly browned before adding to the gravy.
*   **Dairy-Free Version:** For those avoiding dairy, substitute the yogurt with a dairy-free alternative (like coconut yogurt), and use coconut cream or full-fat coconut milk instead of heavy cream. Ghee can be replaced with a plant-based oil.
*   **Nut-Free Option:** If you have a nut allergy, you can omit the cashews. To maintain the gravy's thickness and richness, you can use a small amount of poppy seeds, melon seeds, or even a teaspoon of cornstarch slurry (mixed with a little water) added at the end.
*   **Spice Level Adjustment:** For more heat, increase the amount of red chili powder or add a finely chopped green chili during the onion sautéing stage. For a milder version, reduce the chili powder.
*   **Healthier Twist:** Use lean chicken breast, reduce the amount of butter and cream, and consider blending in some roasted red bell peppers with the tomatoes for added nutrients and color without compromising flavor too much.

Mastering homemade Butter Chicken is a culinary reward that promises a deeply satisfying and flavorful meal. This iconic Indian lunch recipe, with its tender chicken and luxurious gravy, is more than just a dish; it's an experience. With these detailed instructions and tips, you're well on your way to creating a Murgh Makhani that will impress and delight everyone at your table. Enjoy the journey into the heart of Indian flavors!
